title: CellPaint-POSH screening links AURKAIP1 knockout with reduced mitochondrial abundance and mTORC1 signaling
summary: Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes. Follow-up AURKAIP1 knockout in A549 cells reduced the mitochondrial marker TOMM20 and pS6, an mTORC1 activity readout, relative to control. The authors propose that mitochondrial translation/metabolism may influence mTORC1, while the causal pathway remains unresolved.
ai_technology: CellPaint-POSH with CP-DINO-1640 self-supervised embeddings and a vision transformer

evidence.tested: Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes.
evidence.unknown: The result is from an A549 cell-line knockout study and supports an association between AURKAIP1 loss, reduced mitochondrial abundance and reduced pS6; it does not establish the molecular mechanism or direct causal pathway between mitochondrial function and mTORC1. The arrayed follow-up used two technical replicate wells per knockout, was not randomized or blinded, and is not an independent replication. The paper identifies HSD17B10 as a previously reported mTORC1 regulator; this record focuses on AURKAIP1.
evidence.ai_role: CP-DINO self-supervised embeddings and morphological similarity analysis of pooled CRISPR knockout profiles identified AURKAIP1 in a cluster with mitochondrial and pS6 phenotypes, prioritizing it for follow-up. The authors then used arrayed RNP knockout and TOMM20/pS6 staining; those assays showed reduced mitochondrial abundance and pS6 after AURKAIP1 knockout. The model enabled candidate prioritization, while the perturbation and marker measurements supplied the specific experimental evidence.
